svg.text: EscolaViva — The domain layer, block by block
apps/api/src/*/domain/ · 17 files, 4 bounded contexts · none imports a database, HTTP, a log, a scheduler or a third-party library
who signs in, with what role, at which school
School { id, networkId, name, inepCode, active }
User { id, networkId, name, email, cpf, phone, active }
Session { id, networkId, userId, createdAt, expiresAt, ip }
Read views built from the entities
only when the DATABASE returns a value outside the domain
who studies, where and with whom
ClassGroup { schoolId, academicYearId, name, gradeLevel, shift }
ACTIVE_ENROLLMENT_STATUS — the constant writers spell it with
Read views built from the entities
TeacherClassGroupSubject — the same, plus class group and shift
grade, attendance and the closing of the term
Domain services — the core of the module
what the school tells families, and who read it
withAuthor(stored, authorName) ← builds the read view
Shared kernel — the four things the domain is allowed to reach, and nothing else
The only value object with arithmetic of its
It lives in shared/ because the rule is the
SAME for identity and academics. Duplicating
it would be worse than sharing it.
An expected failure is a VALUE, not an
exception. The domain does not use it: a
predicate returns a boolean, the application
No domain file imports one yet. The
permission is written down anyway, so that
the day a rule needs the clock, the rule is
not what stops it — and reading the real
clock stays an effect behind a port.
constants.ts — shared and the module's own
Added to the permission so a limit with an
owner does not have to be copied into
domain/ to stay reachable. It is the one
concession, and it carries no behaviour.
The rule that draws this boundary — apps/api/.dependency-cruiser.js
Written as a PERMISSION, not a denylist. A denylist only forbids what
somebody remembered to name: shared/pagination and shared/config were
never on one, and a domain file importing either would have passed the
check in silence. Not a convention — `bun run check` breaks the build.
That is why zod appears in 18 use cases and in zero file under domain/.
The style: anaemic record + pure function
No entity is a class. They are all type X = { ... }, and behaviour
lives in an exported function that takes the record:
Accepted consequence: there is no encapsulation. Nothing stops
building an Enrollment with an inconsistent status — the guarantee
comes from the database CHECK and from the predicate the use case
In exchange: every rule is a pure function, testable without
building an object, without mocks and without a database. The 17
files under domain/ import NOTHING beyond their own module's
It is tactical DDD in a functional style. Calling it an “anaemic
model” is only a criticism when the rule leaks into the service —
here it does not: it is in domain/, and the check says so.
Where failure comes out — three channels, never mixed
isValidGradeValue(11) → false. It does not throw, does not format
a message, does not know what a form field is.
2. Result<T> (application/) — the EXPECTED failure becomes a value.
fieldFailure(field, code, message): 52 call sites across the 17
use-case files that import it. A grade out of range, a duplicate
enrollment, a term already closed: none of that is an exception,
Returned from inside unitOfWork(), it is also what rolls the
transaction back — and with it the idempotency claim, so a refused
submission does not burn the client's key.
Forbidden (0 uses, declared and never thrown).
And two exceptions in the domain itself: toRole() and
toNetworkStatus(). They fire only if the DATABASE returns a value
outside the set — corruption, not a user error.
What this domain does NOT have
AGGREGATE ROOT as an object. There is no class holding children
and refusing an invalid change. The aggregate's boundary is the
module's index.ts plus the repository: whoever is outside only
DOMAIN EVENTS. Zero. No event is created, published or consumed
anywhere under apps/api/src. unitOfWork was written as the only
commit point precisely so that the outbox, when it exists, goes in
there and nowhere else — but it does not exist yet.
REPOSITORY IN THE DOMAIN LAYER. There is no repository interface
under domain/. The repositories live in infra/ and take the
transaction's `sql` as a parameter. Dependency inversion exists
SPECIFICATION, POLICY, SAGA. None of those patterns shows up —
and nothing in the code pretends they do.
ANTI-CORRUPTION LAYER. academics takes Role from identity as is;
assessment consumes Enrollment and ClassGroupSubject untranslated.
identity is the leaf: it knows nobody.
PUBLISHED LANGUAGE — the crossing is always through index.ts.
domain/, application/ and infra/ are private, and depcruise
It is a Conformist relationship over published language, not an
ACL: cheap now, and the bill Stage 14 will pay.
THE INVERSION THE DATABASE USED TO IMPOSE is gone: app_user no
longer points at academics. student_guardian.user_id points the
other way, and identity is a leaf there too. See the ER.
A second rule guards the layer above: no-sdk-in-application lets
a use case name exactly one third-party package — zod. Anything
else asking to be added is an effect, and an effect belongs
